title: Ex-Rockstar Boss Dan Houser Won't Play GTA 6 – And For Good Reason
description: Former Rockstar boss and GTA creative director Dan Houser reveals he doesn't play open-world games and won't play GTA 6, to protect his new projects at Absurd Ventures.
author: GTA6 Hub Editorial
content:
## Protecting the Creative Spark: Why Dan Houser Won't Play GTA 6

For millions of fans eagerly awaiting the next chapter in Rockstar Games' crown jewel, the idea of skipping *Grand Theft Auto 6* is almost unimaginable. Yet, that is precisely what Dan Houser, the former co-boss of Rockstar Games and former creative director on the *Grand Theft Auto* series, plans to do.

In reports from IGN Games, it was revealed that Houser not only avoids playing a lot of open-world games in his daily routine, but he also has no intention of playing *GTA 6* when it arrives. While this might come as a shock to fans who associate him so closely with the franchise, the decision stems from a very deliberate and positive creative rationale.

### A Clean Slate for Absurd Ventures

Houser has officially moved on from his monumental tenure at Rockstar and is now fully invested in his new enterprise, **Absurd Ventures**, where he is currently working on two new game projects.

The core reason behind his decision to steer clear of *GTA 6* and other open-world giants is simple: **creative preservation**. Houser does not want his own creative vision and the development of his new projects to be influenced, consciously or subconsciously, by contemporary open-world blockbusters.

In the high-pressure environment of game development, maintaining an untainted, independent perspective during the ideation phase is crucial. By deliberately detaching himself from the industry's benchmark titles, Houser ensures that the universes being built at Absurd Ventures remain uniquely fresh and untethered from past formulas.

### The Legacy and the Future

Dan Houser helped define what open-world gaming could achieve over decades at Rockstar Games, setting narrative and structural standards that the industry still follows today. By choosing to look forward rather than backward—even when it means ignoring the most anticipated sequel of the decade—he demonstrates the discipline of a master storyteller looking to reinvent his craft.

## Editor's Take

Dan Houser's refusal to play *GTA 6* isn't a snub; it's the ultimate expression of creative discipline. By intentionally shielding his mind from the industry's biggest open-world juggernauts, he is clearing the canvas for Absurd Ventures. It's a bold reminder that true innovation requires stepping away from past triumphs to discover what lies beyond.
